observations: Television screen displaying a PlayStation 4 (PS4) dashboard menu.
Game icons for 'EA SPORTS FC 25', 'Grand Theft Auto V', 'God of War', 'Mortal Kombat 11', and 'Sekiro' are visible.
The system status in the top right corner indicates 'Offline'.
A watermark 'KEVIN VIDEOS GAMES AND' is visible across the center of the image.
No physical console hardware, cables, or controllers are shown in the photo.

claims.claim: Hacked and install games on your ps4 console software version 12.02
claims.evidence: Public technical data for the PlayStation 4 modding scene confirms that jailbreaks/hacks are only available for firmware versions up to 11.00. Version 12.02 is currently unhackable.

claims.claim: or any software below than that
claims.evidence: While versions 11.00 and below are hackable, the photo does not show the 'System Information' screen to verify the firmware of the console pictured.

risks.risk: The advertised service for firmware 12.02 is a known scam pattern.
risks.proof: A video showing the console's 'System Information' screen at version 12.02 with a functional homebrew enabler (e.g., GoldHEN) active.

risks.risk: The physical existence and condition of the console are not established.
risks.proof: Photos of the physical console unit showing the model number and serial sticker.

proof_requests: Video of the console's 'System Information' screen showing the firmware version.
Photos of the physical PS4 console unit being offered.
Proof of the jailbreak (e.g., Debug Settings or GoldHEN menu) functioning on the claimed firmware.
response.reason: The seller claims to be able to hack PS4 firmware version 12.02. Currently, there is no public jailbreak for any version above 11.00. This is a common fraudulent claim used to solicit payments for non-existent services.
